newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends slightly up on cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends slightly up on cautious mood.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly up on Tuesday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), but long liquidation erased most of the early gains, brokers said.
They said that after several days of rises, the chance of a technical correction had increased and this led to some long liquidation.

Trading was open as usual from 9.00 a.m. to 9.40 a.m. (0100-0140 GMT), but the two sessions between 9.45 a.m. and 10.55 a.m. (0145 GMT and 0255 GMT) were cancelled for the funeral ceremony of leader Deng Xiaoping, who died last Wednesday.
The funeral started at 10.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) and lasted for nearly an hour. It was broadcast live on nationwide television.
The key May 1997 copper contract ended at 23,390 yuan ($2,820) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened up at 23,440 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,480 and a low of 23,330.
March rose 10 yuan to 23,170, April fell 20 to 23,290, June put on 20 to 23,400 and July 10 to 23,400. August was unchanged at 23,400.
Combined volume fell to 47,290 tonnes from 94,470.
Copper opened higher but long liquidation pushed prices off highs, and they moved at low levels for most of the session.
"Few investors are willing to buy at such high levels," said one trader. "They are waiting for a technical correction after the continued rises of the past few days."

Analysts said they expected copper to fall in the short term, but most of them believed copper was likely to strengthen again after any correction because China's peak copper consumption period is nearing.
Aluminium ended up. March rose 70 yuan to 15,700 per tonne, April 130 to 16,050, May 160 to 16,380 and June 270 to 16,500. Combined volume rose to 3,460 tonnes from 1,500.
